what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission approved a waiver of easement for a sewer connection at 44 Northfield Road across 34 Northfield Road; the chair announced approval, count not audible.
The commission voted to prorate by month the first-quarter bill of a new owner at 136 Leominster Road, who had been billed a full quarterly minimum.
Three ARPA proposals from sewer, covering manholes, pump stations and a mobile generator, go to the Select Board on November 1; spending would fall in the next two fiscal years.
The business manager will consult town counsel before camera inspections of clay laterals are pursued, and will gather replacement cost estimates.
The commission aims to bring its batch of sewer policy changes to one public hearing by around year end, and set the next meeting for October 25.

why_it_matters: A new owner billed a full quarter's minimum charge for part of a quarter now gets a monthly proration, which touches the sewer bill of anyone who buys a home mid-quarter.
The ARPA requests and clay lateral replacement estimates bear on how sewer upgrades are paid for, whether from one-time federal money or from sewer rates and property owners.
The batch of sewer policy changes is slated for a public hearing, where residents on the sewer system could comment on rules that affect their bills.
watch_next: November 1: the Select Board is to discuss the three sewer ARPA proposals.
October 25: the next Sewer Commission meeting, run by a member in the chair's absence.
